# Wildbox: Full Context for Language Models

> Wildbox is an open-source (MIT), self-hosted security operations platform run with Docker Compose. An OpenResty gateway sits in front of Python microservices for identity, security tools, threat intelligence data, vulnerability management, cloud security posture management (CSPM), incident response playbooks and optional AI-assisted analysis, with a Next.js dashboard. The project is in an early evaluation phase. Author: Fabrizio Salmi.

Every fact below was taken from the repository (https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/wildbox): ports and service names from `docker-compose.yml`, routes from `open-security-gateway/nginx/conf.d/wildbox_gateway.conf`, the login flow from the integration tests. Where this file and the repository disagree, the repository is right. Versions and release notes are in CHANGELOG.md; this file deliberately does not state a version.

## What Wildbox Is Not

- Not a SIEM: there is no log search engine or event correlation.
- Not a WAF: the gateway authenticates, rate-limits and routes; it does not filter attacks.
- No local LLM runtime: AI analysis uses the Anthropic API when enabled.
- No Kubernetes manifests: deployment is Docker Compose.

## Architecture

```
Client (browser, CLI)
   |
   | HTTPS :443   (:80 and :8080 serve /health, redirect the rest to HTTPS)
   v
gateway (OpenResty): TLS, JWT / API-key validation via identity, per-team rate limits
   |
   +-- /auth/jwt/..., /auth/register,
   |   /auth/forgot-password, /auth/reset-password --> identity /api/v1/auth/...
   +-- /auth/users/...        --> identity   /api/v1/users/...
   +-- POST /auth/logout      --> identity   /api/v1/auth/logout
   +-- /api/v1/identity/auth/...--> identity /api/v1/auth/...
   +-- /api/v1/identity/...   --> identity   /api/v1/...
   +-- /api/v1/tools[/...]    --> tools API  /api/tools/...
   +-- /api/v1/tasks[/...]    --> tools API  /api/tasks/...  (asynchronous tool runs)
   +-- /api/v1/data/...       --> data       /api/v1/...
   +-- /api/v1/guardian/...   --> guardian   /api/v1/...
   +-- /api/v1/responder/...  --> responder  /v1/...
   +-- /api/v1/agents/...     --> agents     /v1/...  (/api/v1/agents/stats --> /stats)
   +-- /api/v1/cspm/...       --> cspm       /api/v1/...
   +-- /                      --> dashboard (Next.js)

identity, data and guardian keep their data in PostgreSQL 15; queues,
token revocations, scan and run state live in Redis 7. Neither publishes
a host port.
```

Every `/api/v1/<service>/` route except identity's requires authentication at the gateway; identity validates tokens itself, apart from `/api/v1/identity/health` (identity's `/health`), which the gateway authenticates. Any other path under `/api/` returns 404, the removed alias `/api/tools/` included; `/tools/`, where a standalone tools UI used to be, returns 404 too. The sensor's local API is not routed through the gateway; the sensor itself is a client of it.

## Services and Ports

The gateway is the only service published on all interfaces. Every other published port is bound to `127.0.0.1`, for health checks and debugging on the Docker host.

| Compose service | Host port | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gateway | 443, 80, 8080 (8081 internal, not published) | OpenResty ingress, TLS, authentication, rate limiting, routing; port 8081 takes identity's auth-cache purge on the Compose network |
| identity | 127.0.0.1:8001 | Users, JWT login and revocation, API keys, teams (FastAPI, fastapi-users) |
| api (tools) | 127.0.0.1:8000 | Runs 52 security tools through an API; Celery workers (`tools-worker`), Flower on 127.0.0.1:5555 |
| data | 127.0.0.1:8002 | Threat intelligence (IOCs, denylists) collected from 7 public feeds by `data-scheduler` |
| sensor | 127.0.0.1:8004 | Endpoint telemetry with osquery, posted in batches through the gateway to the data service's ingest endpoint with a team member's API key (`SENSOR_DATA_LAKE_API_KEY`, scope `data:ingest`); data stores telemetry and sensors per team. Without a key the sensor runs and forwards nothing |
| agents | 127.0.0.1:8006 | Optional AI-assisted IOC analysis with the Anthropic API (Claude) |
| guardian | 127.0.0.1:8013 | Assets, vulnerabilities, remediation, compliance, reporting (Django REST) |
| responder | 127.0.0.1:8018 | YAML incident-response playbooks executed through connectors |
| cspm | 127.0.0.1:8019 | 22 configuration checks against live AWS accounts, run by `cspm-worker`; GCP and Azure scans are refused with 400, and `GET /api/v1/cspm/providers` lists the providers that can be scanned. Reference: https://www.wildbox.io/api/cspm/endpoints/ |
| dashboard | 127.0.0.1:3000 | Next.js web UI, normally reached through the gateway |
| automations | 127.0.0.1:5678 | n8n, only with `--profile automations` |
| prometheus | 127.0.0.1:9090 | Only with `--profile monitoring` |
| alertmanager | 127.0.0.1:9093 | Receives the alerts Prometheus fires; only with `--profile monitoring` |
| postgres, wildbox-redis | none | Datastores |

Canonical page: https://www.wildbox.io/guides/ports/

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/wildbox.git
cd wildbox
make generate-secrets      # scripts/generate_secrets.py writes .env with random secrets
# edit .env: set INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL
make validate-secrets      # refuses placeholders
docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 600
```

There are no default credentials. `scripts/generate_secrets.py` generates every secret, including `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; the identity service creates the first administrator from `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` on first start. Production uses `make start-prod` (adds `docker-compose.prod.yml`). The gateway generates a self-signed development certificate in `open-security-gateway/ssl/` if none is provided.

## Authentication

```bash
env_value() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" .env | head -1; }
CA=open-security-gateway/ssl/wildbox.crt
TOKEN=$(curl -s --cacert "$CA" -X POST https://localhost/auth/jwt/login \
  --data-urlencode "username=$(env_value INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL)" \
  --data-urlencode "password=$(env_value INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD)" | jq -r .access_token)
curl -s --cacert "$CA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://localhost/api/v1/identity/users/me
```

- Login is form-encoded (`username`, `password`) and returns `access_token`. Tokens are HS256 JWTs valid for 30 minutes (`jwt_access_token_expire_minutes`; Compose does not pass an override); there is no refresh endpoint.
- `POST /auth/logout` or `POST /auth/jwt/logout` with the bearer token revokes it: its `jti` is blacklisted in Redis until it would have expired, identity refuses it, and identity purges it from the gateway's authorization cache through the gateway's internal listener on port 8081 (Compose network only, not published). Logout revokes only the token presented.
- Failed-login lockout: after 5 failed password logins for an email (registered or not), login answers 429 with `Retry-After: 900` for 15 minutes, even with the correct password; a successful login before that clears the counter. A wrong current password on change-password, account deletion or an email change counts towards the same lock. The gateway also rate-limits `/auth/jwt/` per client address.
- Changing a password (`POST /api/v1/identity/admin/me/change-password` with `current_password` and `new_password`) ends every session of the account and answers with a new access token; `PATCH /auth/users/me` refuses a password. New passwords must be 12 to 128 characters, must not contain the email address and must not be a common password.
- An account a team owner or admin created must change its initial password first: until it does, identity and the gateway answer 403 `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` to everything but reading the account, changing the password and logging out.
- Passwords are hashed with Argon2id through fastapi-users' `PasswordHelper`; older bcrypt hashes still verify.
- The gateway calls identity with a 5-second timeout, caches authorization decisions for 300 seconds (`AUTH_CACHE_TTL`), and opens a circuit breaker for 60 seconds after 10 failed calls.
- Every FastAPI service (identity, tools, data, responder, agents, cspm) serves `/openapi.json`, and `/docs` and `/redoc` where it has them, only when `ENVIRONMENT` is `development` (the generated `.env` sets `production`), and only on its own port, not through the gateway.
- API keys: create with `POST /api/v1/identity/api-keys` (with a bearer token), send as `X-API-Key`. Every route the gateway authenticates (tools, tasks, data, guardian, responder, agents, cspm and `/api/v1/identity/health`) accepts a bearer token or an API key; identity's own routes (`/auth/users/...`, `/api/v1/identity/...`) take the bearer token only.
- The gateway limits each team to `RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR` requests per hour (default 10,000), enforced per minute (1/60 of it in each 60-second window, 166 by default), and reports the limit in `X-RateLimit-*` headers. A value that is not a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000,000 stops the gateway at start-up.

## Network Targets of the Security Tools

The network tools (port and vulnerability scanners, TLS and certificate analyzers, `network_scanner` and others) refuse internal targets (a synchronous run answers 400, an asynchronous task ends `failed`): private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved and shared addresses, ranges that contain one, names that resolve to one or do not resolve, and the stack's own service names. A range holds at most 1,024 addresses. An operator allows an internal lab with `TOOLS_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_TARGETS` in `.env` (comma-separated CIDR ranges, IP addresses and exact host names; a bad entry stops `api` and `tools-worker` at start-up). Details: https://www.wildbox.io/guides/deployment/#internal-targets-of-the-network-tools

## AI Analysis

The agents service calls the Anthropic API when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL` defaults to `claude-opus-4-8`). Indicators submitted for analysis are then sent to Anthropic. Without a key, analysis tasks fail and the rest of the platform is unaffected.

## Security

- Report vulnerabilities as described in SECURITY.md (https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/wildbox/blob/main/SECURITY.md) and https://www.wildbox.io/.well-known/security.txt.
- Known open issues and how each check was made: https://www.wildbox.io/security/status/
